title: Jude and the Vector
premise: Vesper Yarrow smuggles stolen memories in sealed neural vials past the orbital customs of Ceres Gate, and alone he tends a navigation beacon whose original commissioning records have been erased from every archive. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew aged backward into childhood, carrying a message encoded in their restored memories, Vesper discovers his beacon was built to receive it — and that he himself is the smuggled inheritance of the man who commissioned it. To deliver the message that could end the decades-long war between Earth and the Belt, Vesper must surrender every memory he has ever carried, including his own identity. He does, and the war ends; what remains of Vesper is a stranger who tends the beacon, remembering nothing but why it matters.
about_author: Vesper Winterbourne is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for stations she now refuses to name. She writes science fiction about people who keep systems running long after everyone forgets why.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Self
chapters.summary: Vesper runs a shipment of black-market memories through Ceres Gate customs, hiding vials inside a coffin of frozen dead. His POV establishes his trade, his cynicism, and his solitary ritual: winding the ancient beacon on the station's dark side, which no record says anyone owns. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Ship That Sailed Backward
chapters.summary: The Halcyon docks unannounced, its forty crew members children in adult-sized vacsuits, biologically aged backward by decades. Station authorities quarantine the ship; Vesper, bribed to retrieve one child's personal effects, touches the girl's memory vial and glimpses a star chart no living navigator knows. POV: Vesper. Beat: wonder cracking through his armor.

chapters.title: Customs, Interrogation
chapters.summary: Earth's naval intelligence arrives and seizes the Halcyon, interrogating the crew-children who can only babble fragments. Vesper realizes the fragments match transmissions his beacon has been silently receiving for years. A customs officer, Ilsa Reyes, suspects him and offers protection in exchange for the truth he doesn't have. POV alternates Vesper and Reyes. Beat: paranoia tightening.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper pries open the beacon's maintenance hatch and finds a neural interface built for exactly one person — and it accepts him without hesitation. Inside, he experiences fragmented first-person memories of the beacon's commissioner: a man named Yarrow, dying, smuggling something into a newborn. POV: Vesper, disoriented secondhand memories. Beat: the floor drops out of his identity.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Vesper confronts the implication: he may be a manufactured person, grown from the commissioner's pattern to complete a delivery. Reyes finds him at the beacon and, instead of arresting him, reveals naval command wants the Halcyon's message destroyed — it names the atrocity that started the war. Beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Forty Children
chapters.summary: Vesper and Reyes smuggle the Halcyon's crew-children out of quarantine before naval command can 'relocate' them. The eldest, a nine-year-old with an old man's eyes, tells Vesper the message isn't data — it's testimony, and it must be delivered by someone who chooses to carry it. POV: shared. Beat: reluctant responsibility becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Fleeing toward the beacon's relay coordinates aboard a scavenged tug, they're ambushed by a Belt privateer crew who want the message as a weapon. Vesper bargains using smuggler's craft, buying passage by promising the Belt a copy — knowing a copy could reignite everything. Beat: moral compromise souring victory.

chapters.title: Time Running Out
chapters.summary: The message decays as the children's restored memories destabilize; within days the testimony will be unrecoverable. Naval forces close in. The eldest child begins forgetting her own name and asks Vesper to hold her memories too — he refuses, then understands: carrying others' memories is what he was made for. Beat: acceptance of purpose.

chapters.title: Delivery
chapters.summary: At the beacon's full power, Vesper interfaces completely, taking the entire testimony into himself and broadcasting it fleet-wide — every atrocity, both sides', unedited. The navies stand down mid-approach. But the transmission consumes his stored self: his name, his memories, his twenty years of small kindnesses. Beat: climax — sacrifice made real, not sentimental.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Weeks later, a man with no past winds the beacon on Ceres Gate's dark side. The crew-children, growing forward again, visit him with stories of a smuggler named Vesper Yarrow, and he listens like hearing about a stranger he almost misses. Reyes brings him coffee and doesn't explain how she knew he'd like it. Beat: quiet resolution — inheritance continues, identity rebuilt from what we choose to keep.
